title: Frontiers: Polarized America: From Political Polarization to Preference Polarization
authors: Verena Schoenmueller; Oded Netzer; Florian Stahl
eligible_reason: Not staggered. All regressions use a single common pre/post date around the 2016 presidential election (pre_post = month > 10 on Twitter, month_year > 11 in Nielsen, dummy_pre_post_election in YouGov). Twitter: xtreg democratic_basket i.pre_post##i.democrat c.month##i.democrat, fe (user FE, party-specific linear trends, no calendar-time FE). Nielsen Tables 3-4: pre_post x continuous county Clinton vote share with share-specific trends and a price control. YouGov: pre_post x democrat with month x democrat. BrandEvents.csv lists brand political events but is used only in descriptive figures.
design_notes: Stata (Twitter, Nielsen, YouGov do-files), R for Figures 1-5, Python for Nielsen extraction. Twitter user-month panel of followers of either party (TwitterBasket_2016_2017_2018.csv, wide format). Cluster user_id or store.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: single common post date (2016 election); party x post with party-specific linear trends; no calendar-time FE
continuous Clinton vote share x post with share-specific trends and price control; data not shipped
common post date; data not shipped

data_files_note: Twitter data shipped (anonymized user IDs, 242 MB); Nielsen and YouGov data must be acquired from Kilts and YouGov.
data_provenance_note: Twitter panel with anonymized user ids; Nielsen/YouGov not shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex metadata (no article text). Election is a single common event; no staggered adoption.
